The hug: stronger contact and reciprocal stress tests

49 completed configurations plus 2 finer-mesh continuations. No object or square-wall penetration in the final protocol. Smallest certified swept clearance: 0.0101661. Largest scaled energy error: 8.50815e-05.

Contact springs have been replaced by barriers and guarded adaptive steps. Whole segments and separation between the material boundaries are checked. The material still yields and keeps a fading rest-shape imprint. Default contact introduces a small stand-off gap and changes the contact response.

Numerical and geometric checks

17 analytic/gradient/domain checks, including active self-contact and the recorded crossing, independent DOP853 integrations, step/tolerance refinement, zero-port controls, meshes with 24/48/72 angles, and lobed contact subdivisions with 8/16/32 pieces. Proper crossings of nonadjacent mesh edges were checked at every saved frame. Swept certificates check obstacle exclusion, boundary separation and triangle orientation along accepted straight steps.

The hardest case and its practical limit

The combined extreme one-way test completed time 1, with no overlap, but its smallest swept triangle area was 1.0794% of reference area, close to the 1% stop threshold. It required 148168 accepted half steps, 30031 rejected trials, and a smallest half step of 3.87073e-07. The playback includes this severe deformation. Completing the test does not establish unlimited robustness or realistic physical clay.

What these results establish

The numerical hug can react back on the Lorenz drive through an explicit work-balanced port. The repaired boundary excludes the fixed objects under the tested forcing. Effects on variability depend on initial state and time window. Refinement agreement supports numerical reliability for the tested equations.

This remains a dimensionless 2-D prototype without friction, fracture, physical clay calibration or experimental measurements. Finite runs do not prove universal stability, global existence, or any Navier–Stokes theorem. Older inaccurate and interrupted attempts remain under initial attempts and weak-barrier attempts.
